title: Nicolas Raince (Rome) to Montmorency and François I, eight letters
correspondents: Nicolas Raince → Montmorency; → François I
status: Attempted 17 Sept 2026 (targets/raince/): Tomokiyo's 1526 key re-measured off his table image and applied glyph by glyph to the 13 May (pp. 29-31) and 20 Nov 1526 (p. 105) passages. Removed from the catalogue when first claimed read in part; restored 23 Oct 2026: Reading audit 22-23 Oct 2026 (George Lasry's test: a reading must build sentences): the passages decode into clauses broken by unresolved stretches in nearly every line, so nothing counts as read. The other letters of the entry carry contemporary interlinear or printed decipherments (Mignet 1886, Bourrilly 1901, DECODE 3696); the open residue is the unglossed part of no. 7 (13 May) and of no. 24 (20 Nov). 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (pull request #163): the 20 Nov residue read, p. 105 lower and the whole of p. 106 (a page of cipher not treated before), about 98% of words with Tomokiyo's table. Entry narrowed: the open residue is the unglossed part of no. 7 (13 May, pp. 29-31).
why: League of Cognac, the Colonna raid on Rome (Sept 1526), prelude to the Sack; Aug 1529 = Cambrai and Bologna.
score_note: Eight letters in presumably one system give enough text for a statistical attack; no key in print that we know of.
verify: Re-read the unresolved glyphs of pp. 29-31 and p. 105 on full-resolution crops; collect the two word signs from the glossed letters nos. 6, 8, 10, 28.
known: Tomokiyo's 1526 key fits after re-measuring (raince.html); the clear close of 13 May transcribed.
open: No. 7 (pp. 29-31) and no. 24 (p. 105), the unglossed lines: unresolved glyphs (~13% of letters) and two word signs absent from Tomokiyo's key; no sentence builds through.

title: Hieronimo Ranzo (?) to 'Garbino', intercepted imperial letter
correspondents: Hieronimo Ranzo (probably; Gattinara's man) → 'Garbino'
shelfmark: BnF fr. 3022 no. 20 (ff. 44r–46v; addition sheet and jargon ff. 48–50v)
status: The other two items first catalogued here (nos. 6 and 10, del Vasto to Charles V) are read: no. 10 by Lasry (2023) with Tomokiyo's edited text, no. 6 in targets/vasto1527/ (its own page since 14 Oct 2026). No. 20 is an Italian letter, Madrid 11 Apr 1528, to 'Garbino', in the same code as Hieronimo Ranzo's letters (fr. 2988). The code is initial letter + number with non-alphabetical numbering; ~3,900 groups are transcribed. The key was recovered from the ciphertext by George Lasry and, independently, by Paolo Rosson (6 Oct 2026; PRs #35, #45), and no. 20 measures 94.4% (targets/ranzo1528/, 18 Oct 2026), just under the read bar. No French decipherment exists; Clair. 327 ff. 279-280 is an undeciphered copy.
why: Five months after the Sack of Rome, during Lautrec's campaign in Italy.
score_note: Large one-part-looking code, one letter, no key; see targets/ranzo1528/NOTES.md.
verify: Look for Ranzo's key or a deciphered Ranzo letter (Simancas, Vienna HHStA) before any statistical attack.
known: No. 6 (del Vasto, Cipher 2) deciphered here with Lasry's key, 98.0% (vasto1527.html); no. 10 (Cipher 1) key recovered by Lasry 2023, read in part with Tomokiyo's text. No. 20: Ranzo's code key recovered from ciphertext only by George Lasry and, independently, Paolo Rosson (6 Oct 2026); no. 20 measured here at 94.4% (ranzo1528.html, PRs #35, #45).
open: No. 20 (Garbino letter): 74 of 1,314 tokens, 27 groups with no value in either key and 47 tentative Lasry values Rosson's key does not confirm; both keys' readings still to be checked against the images of ff. 44r-46v. Blocker: open codes.

title: Charles III of Lorraine to the count of Vaudémont, copy
correspondents: Charles III, duke of Lorraine -> comte de Vaudemont (Tomokiyo's page says Charles II); shelfmark: Tomokiyo cites 'f.125', the stamped folio on the leaf is 109 (canvas 227)
shelfmark: BnF fr. 3621 no. 97 (fol. 109); no. 22 (fol. 31) is the January decipherment
folio_note: canvas = 2 x folio + 9; no. 97 at fol. 109 = canvas 227, no. 22 at fol. 31 = canvas 71; the folio printed before a piece number belongs to it
status: Attempted 18 Sept 2026 (targets/lorraine1592/, PR #4): the reciprocal letter-pair key recovered from the ciphertext alone (Tomokiyo had broken it in 2025 without publishing a text); no. 22 is a plaintext decipherment of the January letter, with no cipher. Removed from the catalogue when first claimed solved; restored 23 Oct 2026: Reading audit 22-23 Oct 2026 (George Lasry's test: a reading must build sentences): no. 97 decodes into fragments with a gap in almost every line, so nothing counts as read.
why: Lorraine's double game between the League and Henri IV. The ciphered passages carry the military business the clear text only skirts: prisoners and munitions, an order to receive the Duke's commandment and to conserve the plain, Chasteauvillain, and the intention to bring the army back into the quarters of La Fauche, between Neufchateau and Chaumont. The clear text around them has the attempt on Chasteauvillain, munitions promised and undelivered, Chaumont and Buzonville; no. 22's decipherment carries the January business - the Spanish march on Rouen, Mayenne finding the Spaniards resolved on battle, Parma's judgement, then the legate, the Spanish pretensions, Villeroy at Pontoise, the house of Bourbon, Bellievre, and the peace.
score_note: If no. 22's decipherment corresponds to a cipher copy elsewhere in the volume the key falls; otherwise a single copy.
verify: Re-read the 42 per-line crops with the recovered key to correct the barred, dotted and capital variants; ask AD Meurthe-et-Moselle for the ducal key.
known: Letter-pair key recovered from the ciphertext alone (lorraine1592.html).
open: Special signs inside words (about 60 tokens), figures 57, 98, 122, 123, 13, 137, 88, 146, 121, 103, garbled runs L12, L13, L20; no sentence builds. Blocker: no key material; a key or duplicate may survive in the Lorraine ducal archive (AD Meurthe-et-Moselle).

correspondents: Johann Loew; "Johann von Alairt"; Jacob Quelwitz → Johann Georg I of Anhalt-Dessau / Peter Meyer
shelfmark: Landesarchiv Sachsen-Anhalt, Z 44 (Abteilung Dessau) A 9a Ic Nr. 1 Bd. I-III, Nr. 2 Bd. I-IV, Nr. 3, Nr. 4 Bd. I, Nr. 5, Nr. 6 (all digitised)
folio_note: Images: https://recherche.landesarchiv.sachsen-anhalt.de/images//Z_44/A_9a_Ic_<volume>/max/Z_44__A_9a_Ic_<volume>__NNNN.jpg (e.g. Nr_2_Bd_I). Keys: Nr. 2 Bd. I image 6, 'Cifra ... Joannis Georgii Principis Anhalt', a sign alphabet a-z and a nomenclator 10-70; Nr. 2 Bd. II image 184, a slip with signs for 11 names and words (37 = Iudaeus, 68 = Einsidell). Alairt's letters from Prague with cipher, deciphered between the lines: Nr. 1 Bd. II images 152-153 (5 Apr 1610), 177 (19 Apr), 197 (4 May), 241-242 (18 May); Nr. 1 Bd. III images 41-42 (May), 154 (July), 263 (Aug). Undeciphered: Nr. 4 Bd. I image 400, an 8-line slip docketed 'praes. Dessau den 23. Novemb. 1611'.
status: Checked image by image by Michael Brackx (issue #128, 27 Oct 2026); images 6, 241 and 400 confirmed here. The cipher in use is Alairt's: German in Latin script with every letter turned top to bottom (b/p, d/q, n/u, m/w trade places; e looks like o). Every cipher line of his 1610 letters has a decipherment in a second hand above it, except formulas. The Nov 1611 slip has none; its first line reads 'Will der Kayser bericht werden, dass der Hertz[og] von Braun[schweig] ...' (Brackx; agreed here). No letter in Nr. 1 Bd. I-III, Nr. 2 Bd. I-II, Nr. 3 or Nr. 4 Bd. I uses the prince's table or the slip key. Not searched: Nr. 2 Bd. III-IV (accounts), Nr. 5-6 (newsletters), Nr. 1 Bd. III image 80 (would not load). Christian I of Anhalt-Bernburg's cipher systems 1608-27 are in Z 18 A 9a Nr. 1/0. Target folder: targets/anhalt1610/ (in progress).
why: Intelligence from Rudolf II's Prague for the Calvinist Anhalt princes before the Union.

title: Lt. Gen. Richard Taylor (Dept. of Alabama, Mississippi and East Louisiana) → Maury, S. D. Lee, Forrest and others: telegram letter-books with Confederate Vigenère passages copied in cipher only
correspondents: Richard Taylor (by W. F. Bullock Jr., AAG) → D. H. Maury (Mobile), S. D. Lee (Augusta), Wirt Adams, Gov. Clark, Richmond and others
shelfmark: NARA RG 109, War Department Collection of Confederate Records, Chapter II vols. 10, 11 and 196 (Telegrams Sent, Department of Alabama, Mississippi and East Louisiana, 1864-1865)
folio_note: Cipher words written in capitals inside the clear copies, word lengths kept. Vol. 196 (Feb-Mar 1865, naId 45485022): about 40 runs, e.g. frame 0061 = p. 117, Taylor → Maury 12 Mar 1865 (viewed). Vol. 11 (1865, naId 12127054): about 10 runs. Vol. 10 (1864-65, naId 16878212): about 8 runs. Run lists with best key per run in research/nara_triage_d/capruns1.txt and capruns2.txt.
status: Not unsolved in the strict sense: the keys are the known Confederate ones. Frame 0061 transcribed from the image and read here with COME RETRIBUTION (Vigenère, key running through the cipher letters only): 'Telegraph in cipher what [cavalry you have on which side of bay, strength and name of commander] ... Direct [cavalry so keep close to enemy] as possible ... [keep in constant telegraphic communication with] Genl D W Adams ... indicate in cipher [what] ... you have decided upon [outside through which to communicate]'. On the OCR alone, runs in vol. 11 read with COME RETRIBUTION ('stores', 'will move westward', 'was evacuated by') and runs in vol. 10 read with COMPLETE VICTORY ('Genl Johnston this alone will restore confidence', 'renders the assignment'). The volumes carry the 'War Records COPIED' stamp, so the Official Records may print these telegrams, but whether OR printed the cipher words deciphered or left them out was not checked. why: A set of Confederate field ciphers from the last months of the war (Mobile campaign, Wilson's raid) that a known key reads, with the clear sense of each telegram in the same book: a quick, verifiable reading and a test set for Confederate key usage (which key, and when the change was made).

verify: Get Schmitz & Winkelmann 1961 for the symbol table; view the Kassel scans of Ms. theol. 181 and Ms. chem. 19.

frame_check.saw: The linked ppnresolver id opens ORKA volume 'Chemische Korrespondenz des Landgrafen Moritz', shelfmark 2 Ms. chem. 19[3 (red cover, cover/prepage/table of contents entries). That is not any of the items the entry names (2 Ms. theol. 181 former cover Bl. 1/2; Popp letters in 2 Ms. chem. 19[2 and 19[5). No cipher page was seen; page text search for Geheimschrift found nothing.
frame_check.note: Catalogue link points to the wrong volume (19[3). ORKA site shows an Anubis proof-of-work page that clears by itself after about 10 s. Need ORKA viewer ids for 19[2, 19[5 and theol. 181.

seen.where: ORKA Kassel viewer, 2 Ms. chem. 19[3 (https://orka.bibliothek.uni-kassel.de/viewer/image/1381745635760/150/ and /134/, /133/); ORKA full-text catalogue search 'Geheimschrift' (9 hits) and the exhibition catalogue 'Alchemie am Kasseler Hof' (Broszinski/Wiedemann 2011) no. 23, viewed in ORKA
seen.extent: Volume 19[3 holds about 50 pages in Geheimschrift (catalogue no. 23: 'Rezepte und Briefe an Landgraf Moritz in Geheimschrift', ff. 62r-62v illustrated). Seen: image 150 (f. 70v), an invented runic-style glyph script in 5 lines with a tipped-in slip carrying a symbol/letter table; ff. 62r-62v are clear German numbered points.
seen.cipher: Invented-alphabet Geheimschrift (letter substitution with a key slip and key lists in the volume, 'Schluessel zu zwei Geheimschriften' per the catalogue); partly published by Schmitz/Winkelmann 1961. No decipherment of the glyph leaves is written on them. The frame check of 30 Oct found the linked volume without a cipher page: that volume is in fact the right one (the record's annotation names theol. 181 as its former cover and Ms. chem. 19[2/[5 as the Popp letters).

prior_art.decode: Not on DECODE (known.py 'chem. 19' and 'Moritz Popp': only this entry and the Europeana sweep).
prior_art.tomokiyo: Not in cryptiana; web searches found no Tomokiyo page for Moritz.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry or DECODE work found on the Kassel alchemical scripts.
prior_art.edition: Schmitz and Winkelmann, 'Ueber die alchemistischen Geheimschriften im Briefwechsel des Landgrafen Moritz von Hessen-Kassel', Pharmazeutische Zeitung 106 (1961) 374-378 (partial publication per the ORKA annotation; article not seen). Broszinski, Manuscripta chemica in quarto (2011) and the 2011 exhibition catalogue describe the volume.
prior_art.literature: Searches: Kassel Ms. chem. 19 Geheimschrift/Popp, Schmitz Winkelmann 1961 (nothing online), 'theol. 181' Kassel; Moran, 'Privilege, communication and chemiatry' (Moritz's circle) is the relevant secondary work.

vetting.key_check: A key to two scripts is in the volume itself (catalogue no. 23, ff. 62r-62v region and the slip on f. 70v); no key is held in the repo. The 1961 article's symbol table was not seen, so how much of the rest is readable with it is unknown.
vetting.duplicates: known.py searches: no duplicate; ORKA lists other Kassel volumes with cipher alphabets (4 deg Ms. chem. 31, 44, 60[5,2) which are separate items.
vetting.closed: Schmitz/Winkelmann 1961 published part of the Geheimschrift pieces and the volume carries its own key material; the rest needs the 1961 table or a rebuild from the in-volume keys.

title: Count Münster's papers on the war between Russia and France: reports from Göteborg, Kolberg, St Petersburg, Dresden and Lisbon, part ciphered and part never deciphered
correspondents: Hanoverian agents (Dörnberg and others) → Count Ernst zu Münster
place: Göteborg; Kolberg; St Petersburg; Dresden; Lisbon
shelfmark: NLA Hannover, Dep. 110 A Nr. 111
folio_note: 277 images; undivided numeric cipher on ff. 141-143 (aufn_0158-0160)
status: Removed 6 Nov 2026 (targets/ompteda1811/): the 'nicht dechiffriert' part is ff. 134v-150 (aufn_0152-0167), the rest of Ludwig von Ompteda's report to Münster, Berlin, 24 July 1811, and its P.S., in 'den deutschen Chiffre von 1790' (two-part 4-digit code, undivided); f. 134 and f. 148 are deciphered between the lines. The full text is printed in F. von Ompteda (ed.), Politischer Nachlaß ... Ludwig von Ompteda, vol. 2 (Jena 1869), nos. 21-22, pp. 51-60 (archive.org 11005674bsb); checked against the cipher on f. 134v. Writer Ompteda, not Dörnberg; the rest of the volume is clear or interlined. Earlier status: Finding aid: "teils chiffriert (ein Teil nicht dechiffriert)". Viewed: ff. 141-143 are unbroken digits with nothing written over them; aufn_0198 has decipherment between the lines.
why: Anglo-Hanoverian secret intelligence against Napoleon in 1810-13, the network behind the German rising.
score_note: Scored from the finding-aid description during the Nov 2026 German portals sweep 2 (research/sweep_2026-11_german_portals_2/); scan viewed
verify: Find all undeciphered pieces; align with the interlined ones for a crib.
